methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict game or series wins beyond team quality?
Can the recommended mix be derived without outcome-derived labels or leakage?
Is a sample of about 54 series enough to detect an adherence-win association?
How should sparse suppression-trigger exposure be handled?

historical_evidence.finding: BEST/AVOID run rates after suppression vs series wins (55 series, n=110 series-directions). Spearman BEST vs won rho=+0.131 p=0.1723; AVOID vs won rho=-0.098 p=0.3099. Recorded verdict 'null', failure type A_unanswerable. INSUFF_EVIDENCE is 91.5% of triggers; BEST was run on 44.7% of triggers but only 9.7% of volume.

Adaptation quality (pct BEST minus pct AVOID) vs series wins, controlling for RS net-rating talent. Talent_diff_z p=0.0213; adapt_diff_z +0.328 p=0.2755 (team-in-series cluster p=0.2449). Univariate adapt beta=+0.311 p=0.1128. The record states n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.

Series-level AVOID share vs winning: rho=-0.26 p=0.07 (n=50), underpowered, with ~80 series stated as needed for p<0.05. The game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008 is flagged as inflated n plus a team-quality confound. Still confounded by team quality (OKC disciplined and good). Verdict inconclusive.

In holdout game-team rows (n=908), games whose mix was closer to the model's recommended mix had higher efficiency. Raw gap +5.18 ORtg; strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg. The outcome was efficiency (ORtg/PPP), not winning, and no CI was stated. Validation was same-pipeline. Model regret is non-negative by construction.
A raw PUTBACK suppression effect collapsed after matching on margin/game state. The original finding was a score/context confound.
Only 2/30 stars had a stable top suppressor across seasons (powered null). Suppression profiles are not stable season to season.
Star suppression profiles: rank-1 deltas mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control.
Sequential suppression cells had n_after of 32-95 against thousands of baseline possessions and no multiplicity correction.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level Spearman of BEST/AVOID run rates against series wins
failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable: n=110 directions gave nonsignificant results, and 91.5% of triggers were INSUFF_EVIDENCE (limitation recorded: small sample).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level logistic of adaptation difference on wins controlling for talent
failed_approaches.why: Adaptation was nonsignificant after talent control. n~55 cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality (limitations recorded: confounding, small sample).
Underpowered at n=50 (~80 series needed) and confounded by team quality. The game-level association was inflated by non-independent n.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Raw suppression effect read as causal
failed_approaches.why: C_artifact: the effect was a score/context confound that vanished under matching.

evidence_establishes: The same or a very similar question (BEST/AVOID adherence vs series wins) was tested on 50-55 series and was recorded as untestable or null/inconclusive, with no significant adherence-win association once talent was considered.
Team talent predicted series wins (p=0.0213, cluster p=0.0095) and adherence did not (p=0.275, cluster p=0.245).
Adherence to the recommended mix was associated with efficiency (ORtg) at game level (FAM:SF-APPM-001, supported, same-pipeline validation), but this was not tested against winning.
Suppression-trigger exposure is sparse (91.5% of triggers INSUFF_EVIDENCE) and suppression profiles are unstable across seasons (FAM:SF-APPA-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: That adherence has no relationship with winning. The records give a small-sample null, not a powered null, and point estimates were positive (rho=+0.131, beta=+0.31 or +0.33 per SD).
Whether the APPM-001 efficiency association holds out of the original pipeline, or converts to wins.
Whether the 2025-26 data change the picture, since the retrieved studies used 50-55 series.
Whether adherence is causal rather than a marker of team quality or game state.
own_inferences: With 54 series, the series-level question is essentially a re-run of FAM:SF-APPS-030/027 with 1-5 more series. It cannot reach useful power: a standardized effect of about r~0.37 or larger would be needed for 80% power, and the observed effects are far smaller.

The recommended mix is model-derived and BEST/AVOID labels are derived from outcome PPP, so adherence may partly encode outcomes (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL). If the mix was fit on the same games, adherence-to-win would be leaky.
Adherence is likely correlated with team quality and game state. Leading teams run different play types, so reverse causation (winning series produce adherent mixes) is plausible.

A game-level or possession-level design with clustering, talent control and a frozen out-of-sample recommender is the only plausible way to get power, but it answers a different question than 'predicts winning' at series level.
The prior positive efficiency result is the only support. Its same-pipeline validation and the by-construction regret reduce how far it should be trusted for win prediction.
uncertainties: Whether the 54 series include partial 2025-26 playoff data (complete only from 2026-06-21, after the question date), which would make the sample unstable.
How the 'recommended mix' is operationalised here (the same recommender as APPM-001 or a new one) and whether it is frozen before the outcome seasons.
Why the count is 54 rather than 55; series inclusion rules may differ.
I did not read the full records (truncated results), so details such as the controls used and the direction coding are unverified.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, a series-level test on 54 series might look worth running. The retrieved records show the same test was already run at n=50-55 and recorded untestable/null/inconclusive, with talent confounding and sparse exposure. That moves the decision from proceed to do_not_proceed for the series-level design, and it motivates a restricted game-level alternative.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series gives roughly 80% power only for a large effect (r~0.37 or more). Prior records needed ~80 series for p<0.05 at rho~0.26, and observed effects were smaller.
Talent and adherence cannot be separated at n~55; talent was significant and adherence was not after control.
91.5% of suppression triggers had insufficient evidence for a recommendation, and BEST was run on only ~9.7% of volume.
BEST/AVOID labels are derived from outcome PPP, so adherence is partly built from outcomes unless the recommender is frozen out of sample.

prior_work.summary: The series-level adherence-wins question was tested at n=50-55 and recorded as untestable/null/inconclusive, with no adherence effect after talent control. A game-level efficiency association was found (supported, same-pipeline). No powered test of adherence against winning exists in the retrieved records.

risks.text: 54 series is underpowered for the plausible effect size; any nonsignificant result would be uninformative.
Team quality, opponent strength and game state (score/margin) drive both play-type mix and winning; the APPS-041 artifact shows the same pattern.
BEST/AVOID classification uses outcome PPP, which creates mechanical association with winning.
If the recommended mix is fit on data that include the evaluation series or games, adherence leaks outcomes. The recommender must be frozen on earlier seasons.
Few suppression triggers have enough evidence to issue a recommendation, so adherence is measured on very few possessions per series.
The adherence index is noisy at series level, and suppression profiles are unstable across seasons (FAM:SF-APPA-058).
Model regret is non-negative by construction (FAM:SF-APPM-001), so a nominal alignment advantage may be partly constructed.
Many adherence definitions (BEST, AVOID, difference, L1 distance) and outcome specifications invite forking paths; earlier families already ran several variants.
Regular-season vs playoff tagging and style differences, and season-to-season changes, limit transferring a recommender across seasons.

design.estimand: Minimum viable test: the association between a pre-specified adherence index (negative L1 distance between actual and recommended play-type mix after suppression triggers, from a recommender frozen on earlier seasons) and game win probability, conditional on pre-game team strength and in-game state. A series-level estimate is secondary and descriptive only.
design.unit: Primary: team-game (clustered by series and team-season). Secondary: series (n=54) as a descriptive check.
design.sample: Recommender trained on 2022-23 through 2023-24 and frozen. Evaluation on 2024-25 and 2025-26 regular season plus playoffs, using only data complete as of the pre-registration freeze (2025-26 playoffs complete 2026-06-21; do not analyse before). Exclude triggers with INSUFF_EVIDENCE rather than imputing recommendations.
design.power: At the series level n=54 gives about 80% power only for r~0.37 or more, so a nonsignificant result is not evidence of no effect. Game-level analysis (thousands of team-games) needs a pre-computed MDE with clustered SEs, reported before unblinding. If the MDE exceeds a practically relevant effect (for example a 1-point win-probability change per SD of adherence), declare the test untestable.
design.controls: Pre-game team strength (prior-season or pre-series net rating, not in-series performance), opponent strength, home court, rest, and score margin/game state at the time of each trigger (matching or fixed effects, given the APPS-041 confound). Adherence is measured on possessions before the outcome-defining period, or the recommender is blind to the evaluation games, so labels are not outcome-derived. Cluster by series and team.
design.falsification: Placebo adherence to a shuffled or opponent-mismatched recommended mix should show no association with winning. Also run a negative-control outcome (for example adherence vs a pre-trigger score margin) and a permutation test of recommended mixes across suppression contexts. If placebo adherence predicts winning equally well, classify as artifact.
design.multiplicity: One primary hypothesis (adherence index to game win, one-sided positive, alpha=0.05). Secondary BEST-rate, AVOID-rate, series-level and efficiency analyses are exploratory, with Holm correction across any reported secondary tests. All adherence definitions are fixed before looking at outcomes.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary adjusted coefficient is positive with a cluster-robust CI excluding 0 AND the placebo adherence coefficient is not significant AND the effect has the same sign in 2024-25 and 2025-26 separately. Rejected if the CI excludes the pre-set minimum relevant effect. Otherwise inconclusive. Do not run the series-level test alone with 54 series, since it repeats FAM:SF-APPS-030/027 without added power.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and derived play-type possession records for 2022-23 through 2025-26. Freeze a snapshot and hash before analysis, and run only after 2025-26 playoffs are complete (2026-06-21). Record the series inclusion list (54 vs the prior 55) and the recommender version used in FAM:SF-APPM-001.

How should the recommended mix be derived without leakage or outcome-derived labels?
Is a sample of 54 series sufficient for testing adherence-to-win association?
How should confounding by team quality and opponent strength be handled?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to pull more family details with a follow-up read on SF-APPS-027 and SF-APPS-030, but the budget allows it and I can also finish directly, so I'll likely wrap up without another read.
